text: A mission never runs without a spend cap, and the cap is never above its ceiling.
Whatever state a mission is in, the operator can get it out of that state from the cockpit: no state is a dead end.

A mission's volume (its work) survives every transition. Missions are not deleted: suspend is the end state until archive exists (decision D-6); archive will stop all costs and keep the results readable.

The status the cockpit shows is the machine's real state: when a machine stops or fails on its own, the platform notices on a timer and updates the status (`mission.reconcile`). Looking at a mission never changes it.
An agent runs at most one turn at a time.
Every turn ends, within the agent's limits and a wall-clock timeout.
No turn starts once the mission's spend has reached its cap.
A pause holds until someone resumes the agent, across any restart of the mission (resume, upgrade, crash).
Agents never act on a teammate. A supervisor agent works with the agents it oversees through the mailbox only.
A recurring schedule fires at most every 5 minutes, whoever creates it.
Recipients are on the mission's roster.
A job runs as its author, with no secrets, whether its author submitted it or scheduled it; a job schedule names only its author.

Objectives and their tasks form one tree (no duplicate ids, unknown parents or cycles), and each is changed only by those entitled to: the objective tree by the copilots; a task by its assignee, its creator, the objective's owner or the mission copilot.
A message wakes its recipient.
Any turn can be reconstructed from what is stored: the prompt and mental map it started from, every model call, every tool call with its arguments and result, its cost, and how it ended.
Each step of a turn (a model answer, a tool result) is stored before the next step starts, so a crash loses at most the step in progress.
An interrupted turn is either resumed from its last stored step or closed with a recorded reason; it is never silently dropped or replayed from the start.
open: Resume from the last stored step (needs tools that are safe to repeat), or close the turn and start a new one

text: Every model call made on a mission's behalf (by an agent, a copilot, a sub-agent, a tool or a job) is recorded with who made it, the model, tokens, cost and time, and its full input and output are kept for the retention period the operator sets.
open: The retention period and where the bodies are kept (MongoDB, the mission's volume, object storage); whether tool results are kept in full

text: Every recorded call's cost counts against its mission's spend.
Once launched, a mission is independent of its template: a change to either never reaches the other.
An upgrade reverts on time, and a mission's upgrades stay within the daily allowance until the operator resets it.
The regions the platform manages are written by the platform only; the agent edits its own sections.
An operator's or a copilot's edit to an agent's mental map never lands during that agent's turn.
An alert is raised once per episode, not on every sample, and the daily report is sent once per user per day, even across restarts.
Every change to a mission's files is attributed to an agent and a turn.
Every piece of state that decides what the platform does next (pauses, holds, cooldowns, claims, queued work) is stored, and rebuilt after a restart.
Every change to a mission by the operator, a copilot or the platform (configuration, cap, schedule, pause, machine) is recorded: who, what, when and why.
Every failure that stops work (a crashed turn, a timeout, a failed delivery, a failed provisioning) is recorded with its reason and reaches the operator.
Every route and Tool API name requires an authenticated caller (a session, the admin key, the mission's monitor token, a job's tool token), except the entry points of the `infrastructure` class.
Every request about a mission is checked against the caller's right to that mission before it reaches the operation's home.
Every database query on mission data is scoped to one mission, and to one user where the data is a user's; input supplies values, never operators or field names.
No secret reaches an agent's or a job's environment, prompt, files or tool results.
No secret value is written to logs, conversations or model-call records.
Every path that comes from input is resolved inside its root, after following symlinks, before it is used.
Every outbound request to a URL an agent or the web can influence is checked against internal addresses, at every redirect.
Every input from outside a component's trust boundary is checked against a schema before it is used.
Text written by agents or taken from the web, when placed in a more privileged actor's context, is marked as data, not instructions.
Content written by agents or taken from the web is escaped or sandboxed wherever the cockpit shows it.
Each agent's tools and jobs run as its own OS user. Only the daemon may use `sudo`, only to become an agent's user, with a minimal environment.

Every change the control copilot makes, and every GitHub write from either copilot, is a proposal the operator confirms. The mission copilot changes only its own mission, within its ceilings, and reports each change to the operator.
